palaver: long, lengthy discussion or formal conference with African chiefs and headmen
cicatrization: deliberate scarring of the skin to make decorative patterns on the body
cicatrizing: making raised decorative scars on the skin by cutting and rubbing in irritants
cicatrice: a decorative scar cut into the skin as a tribal mark
cicatrized: marked with decorative scars made deliberately on the skin
camwood: a red dyewood ground to powder and rubbed on the skin for colour
rouge: red paint or powder applied to the face and body as decoration
anklets: rings or bands of metal, beads or fibre worn around the ankles
dug-out: a canoe hollowed out from a single large tree trunk
paddlers: men who propel canoes forward by working paddles in the water
carrier: a native porter hired to carry loads on the march
carriers: native porters hired to carry loads on foot during a journey
caravan: a long line of travelling porters and their loads on the march
hinterland: the inland region lying behind a coast or river mouth
régime: a system of government or administration, especially an authoritarian one
daysman: an arbitrator or umpire appointed to settle a dispute between parties
sylvan: relating to woods and forests; wooded and rural in character
myriad: a countless or very great number of things
insatiable: impossible to satisfy; constantly craving more of something
indelible: impossible to remove or erase, permanently fixed in the mind
impetus: a driving force or momentum that pushes something forward
circumference: the distance around the outer edge or boundary of a circle
bough: a large branch growing from the trunk of a tree
amidships: in or toward the middle part of a ship or canoe
sentinels: sentries or guards posted to keep watch over a camp
steadfast: firm, loyal and unwavering in purpose or in friendship
philanthropic: motivated by a wish to help and benefit other people
endeavour: an earnest effort or attempt to achieve a particular aim
monopoly: exclusive control of a trade or market by a single holder
despatch: an official written message or report sent to a government
barbarous: cruel and savage, or lacking the refinements of civilization
primitive: belonging to an early, simple stage of human development
tattooing: marking the skin with designs by pricking in coloured pigment
wailing: loud, mournful crying or lamentation, often at a death
fetishes: objects believed to hold magical power or to be inhabited by spirits
deceased: a person who has died recently, the dead person
hostilities: acts of warfare or fighting between opposing sides
cassava: a starchy tropical root plant eaten as a staple food
currency: the money or media of exchange in common use in a country
stern: the rear end of a canoe or boat, where the steering is done
coarse: rough in texture or quality, not fine or delicate
knobs: small rounded lumps or protuberances, often on the skin
proximity: the state of being near to someone or something in space
folklore: traditional beliefs, customs and stories passed down by a people
tribal: relating to a tribe, a group of families sharing customs and leaders
grotesque: strangely distorted or ugly in a way that seems unnatural
witch doctor: a native healer who uses magic and charms to cure or divine
retort: a sharp, quick reply made in response to a remark or charge
orator: a skilled public speaker, especially one who addresses assemblies
sprinkled: scattered thinly over a surface or area in small amounts
sickness: illness or disease affecting the body of a person or community
wounded: injured by a blow, cut or weapon, causing harm to the body
dominions: self-governing territories owing allegiance to the British Crown
cloths: pieces of woven or printed fabric used as clothing or currency
sleeping sickness: a deadly fly-borne tropical disease causing fever and drowsiness
